case_title: Jugendra Singh v. State of U.P.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.376 read with s.511
aggravating_circumstances: Attempt to commit rape on a 9 year old girl and causing her death
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused was prosecuted for attempting to commit rape on a nine-year-old girl and causing her death. The prosecution case was that on the day of the incident, the victim and her younger brother were bathing in a pond near their house. The accused took the girl to a nearby field, removed her undergarment, and flung her on the ground. The girl's cries and her brother's alarm attracted witnesses who rushed to the scene. Upon arrival, the accused was pressing the girl's neck, and by the time the witnesses reached the spot, the girl had already died. The accused was apprehended at the scene. The trial court acquitted the accused, citing discrepancies in witness testimony and contradictions in the evidence. The High Court, however, convicted the accused under sections 302 and 376 of the IPC, read with section 511, and sentenced him to life imprisonment and 10 years rigorous imprisonment, respectively, with both sentences running concurrently.
